text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Scottish/Australian Salvation Army chaplain WILLIAM MacKENZIE was born in 1869. He was known as "Fighting Mac" and reportedly joined in charges at Gallipoli armed with a shovel.

One of Australia's most well-known politicians and prime ministers Sir ROBERT GORDON MENZIES was born in 1894. He was leader of the United Australian Party and then the Liberal Party. He earned the nickname of "Pig-iron Bob" when he sold metal to Japan prior to World War II. He was also noted for his admiration of the British Royal family, especially Queen Elizabeth.

The National Party's oldest member, Grafton cattlegrower CYRIL HERBORN, turns 101. He was born in 1895, was gassed and wounded on the Western Front in France in World War I, and has farmed at Kangaroo Creek near South Grafton for 76 years. He is the sole survivor of the First 33rd Battalion, First AIF.
Spoon-bender and mind reader URI GELLER was born in 1946. He discovered his incredible powers at the age of 16 when he reportedly began to read his mother's mind.

Australian singer with the 'Easybeats' STEVE WRIGHT was born in 1948. He was a founding member of the group in 1964 and they quickly developed into the leading pop group in the country. They went to the UK in 1966. They had international success with "Friday On My Mind" (1966). From 1970 to 1974 STEVE appeared in the Australian version of "Jesus Christ Superstar" and then he had a solo hit with "Evie".
British actress JENNY AGUTTER, whose films included "I Start Counting" and "Walkabout", was born in 1952.

British singer/songwriter BILLY BRAGG was born in 1957. In 1977 he formed the punk R&B band 'Riff Raff', which split up in 1981. He started a solo career and had hits with "She's Leaving Home" (1988). He was arrested in 1984 when taking part in a sit-in against apartheid in front of South Africa House in London.
Canadian keyboard player and songwriter with 'Honeymoon Suite' RAY COBURN was born in 1962.
** EVENTS **
1803 : One of the biggest land deals ever was settled

when the United States paid 15 million dollars to France for more than two million square kilometres. The deal doubled the size of the United States with a stroke of a pen. The Louisiana Purchase, as it was called, marked the end of Napoleon's plans for an empire and made the US one of the largest countries.
1820 : The State of Missouri levied a tax against
bachelors. The statute ordered unmarried men between the ages of 21 and 50 to pay a tax of one dollar a year.
1915 : The Allies began retreating from the Dardanelles

after one of the most costly and ill-managed campaigns of the First World War. The Gallipoli campaign attempted and failed to force the narrows and link up with Russia. The attempt cost the lives of 25,000 men and another 76,000 were wounded, 13,000 were missing and 96,000 became sick. The landing on April 25 saw thousands of New Zealand and Australian troops lost against the strategically positioned Turks.
1924 : ADOLF HITLER was paroled after serving eight
months of a prison sentence imposed for high treason.
1933 : A new dancing duo and film partnership was born

with the success of the movie "Flying Down To Rio". The leading man was FRED ASTAIRE and his co-star was GINGER ROGERS. ASTAIRE was a former vaudeville song and dance man who teamed up with his sister ADELE on stage. His first screen test wasn't the best with the verdict being "can't act, slightly bald, can dance a bit." His pairing with ROGERS ensured further success in a long-running series of movies.
1945 : MUSSOLINI's daughter EDDA was jailed for two years
for aiding Fascism.
1968 : American novelist JOHN STEINBECK died. He won the
Nobel Prize for Literature for books such as "The Grapes of Wrath" and "East of Eden".
1972 : BILLY SNEDDEN was elected leader of the Liberal
Party following the resignation of BILLY McMAHON.
1981 : Poland's ambassador to the United States was
granted political asylum in Washington.
1989 : Troops surrendered to demonstrators in Romania
after four thousand people were killed.
1990 : The UN passed a vote of censure against Israel for
the killing of 21 Arab rioters by Israeli troops on Temple Mount in October 1989.
1991 : President BORIS YELTSIN announced that Russia
wanted to join NATO.
1991 : It was announced that American and Egyptian
archaeologists had discovered a fleet of 500-year-old ships buried 13 kilometres from the Nile.
1994 : The Federal Government renewed ten woodchip export
licences, going against the advice of Environment Minister JOHN FAULKNER. The move was highly unpopular, with Green groups threatening to give their preferences to the Liberals at the next election.
